raw_response:
I'll reason through this as the farmer, then give you my plan.

---

Well, I've been on this land forty years. Seven mouths to feed in the house, though my son and his wife work in town most of the year, so it's really me and my old woman doing most of the work, with family coming back for busy times.

My 13.1 mu is split up. The best 8 mu, the flat piece near the canal, that's my wheat-corn land — been double-cropping there as long as I can remember. About 4 mu on the western edge is drier, so I keep that in cotton. The last 1.1 mu is a small piece I put in mungbean — it's too awkward for the big crops, and mungbean doesn't ask much. My wife likes to have it for the household, and what's left I sell at the market in fall.

**Wheat (the 8 mu).** I plant after the October rains, usually around the tenth month start. I use seed I saved from last year — why pay for seed when last year's grain grew fine? Before planting I plow once and put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu — that's my base. Then when the wheat greens up in spring, I throw on one bag of urea per mu as topdress. Old Wang down the road uses less, says the soil has enough, but I've seen years where skimping cost you, so I stick with what works. I water three times — once before winter, once at greening, once at jointing. Pump water from the well costs money but you can't skip jointing. Last year I got around 450 kg per mu, the year before 470. I'll plan for 450.

**Corn (same 8 mu, after wheat).** The hard part is time — maybe six, seven days between wheat harvest and getting corn in. No plowing, just run the seeder through the straw. I buy hybrid seed every year, that one you can't save. About 15 kg of urea per mu, some at planting and some when the tassels come out. If June is dry I water once. My son comes back for a week to help plant. I expect around 500 kg per mu — corn's been good in recent years.

**Cotton (4 mu).** Plant late April. Cotton's finicky but I know it. Less nitrogen than corn — maybe 12 kg per mu. I water twice, once when the bolls are forming and once later if it's dry. The pesticide's what costs — bollworm, aphids, you have to spray a few times. Cotton prices aren't what they were, but I keep going because my wife and daughter-in-law can pick it in fall and that's family labor. Expect around 250 kg lint per mu.

**Mungbean (1.1 mu).** Plant in June on that small piece. Hardly any fertilizer — mungbean doesn't need it, and it's actually good for the soil. One weeding. Harvest in September. Maybe 90 kg per mu. Mostly for the house.

All told I figure about 8,000 to 9,000 yuan on inputs. That's tight but I've got some savings and the son sends money.
